scenario: AITA for being uncomfortable when my boyfriend speaks Spanish to his family around me? | I’m very rarely with my boyfriend and his family, but the few times I have been, they’d only communicate with one another through Spanish, which is a language I hardly know at all. His whole family speaks English as well, but they choose to speak Spanish to one another around me, which makes me uncomfortable because a lot of times it’s regarding plans we’ve made and then my boyfriend has to turn to me and translate what they’ve all been saying, and often he leaves things out and forgets to tell me those necessary details until later. Now of course I don’t mind if it’s like, his siblings to his mother in a conversation that shouldn’t involve me, but when they’re talking with my boyfriend as he’s sitting right next to me, I just feel weird. I understand it’s their “normal language” as my boyfriend calls it, and I’m not trying to be all up in the business or try to have them change their ways, it just makes me feel left out and extremely confused and even a little awkward... I’ve mentioned it to him and he gets defensive and angry, like they’re not going to change to make me more comfortable. I just feel that if the roles were reversed, I would have my family speak to me in a language my boyfriend would understand so he wouldn’t feel left out or like he’s missing something important. Before anyone tells me to simply learn Spanish, first of all, it’s not that easy and second, I am learning Spanish...trying to at least... I feel like I AM the asshole but I don’t want to be...so someone just tell me, am I the asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being unreasonable or not in this situation with my boyfriend and his family. Let me start by laying out what's happening. So, I don't get to spend much time with my boyfriend and his family, but when I do, they speak Spanish to each other, even though they all know English. This makes me feel uncomfortable because a lot of the time, they're talking about plans we've made, and my boyfriend has to translate for me. But he often leaves things out or forgets to tell me important details until later. That's frustrating because I feel like I'm missing out on important information. I understand that Spanish is their "normal" language, and I'm not trying to make them change how they communicate. But when they're talking with my boyfriend while he's sitting right next to me, it just feels weird. I feel left out and confused, and even a little awkward. I mentioned this to my boyfriend, and he got defensive and angry, saying they're not going to change to make me more comfortable. I wonder if I'm being too sensitive or if I'm overreacting. On one hand, I feel like if the roles were reversed, I would have my family speak in a language my boyfriend understands so he wouldn't feel left out or confused. On the other hand, I'm trying to learn Spanish, but it's not easy, and I'm not fluent yet. Am I being unreasonable? Am I the asshole here? I don't want to be, but I'm not sure how to handle this situation without making things worse between me and my boyfriend or his family. Maybe I should consider why they choose to speak Spanish around me. Is it because they're more comfortable in their native language, or is there something else? Could it be that they don't realize how it makes me feel? Or maybe they think I don't mind since I'm not fluent yet? I also think about how important communication is in a relationship. If they're talking about plans in a language I don't understand, how can I be fully involved in those plans? It feels like I'm being excluded, and that's not fair. But then, I also don't want to impose my language preferences on them. I mean, they have every right to speak their native language, especially in their own family setting. It's a tricky balance between respecting their culture and language and feeling included in the conversation. I guess another angle is how my boyfriend reacts when I bring this up. He gets defensive and angry, which makes me feel like I'm the one in the wrong. But I don't think it's unreasonable to want to feel included and informed about plans that involve me. Maybe I should approach the conversation differently next time. Instead of making it about them changing their behavior, I could express how I feel and ask for their understanding. For example, I could say something like, "I feel left out when you speak Spanish around me, especially when we're talking about plans. Could we find a way to include me in the conversation?" But I'm not sure if that would work, especially since he gets defensive. It might require some compromise from both sides. Maybe they could speak English when I'm around, or at least make an effort to include me in the conversation by translating important parts. I also wonder if there's a cultural aspect to this. In some cultures, family communication in the native language is very important, and switching to another language for outsiders might be seen as disrespectful or unnecessary. So, maybe my boyfriend and his family feel that speaking Spanish is a way to maintain their cultural identity and closeness. But then, in a relationship, there should be some give and take. Both partners should make an effort to include each other in family dynamics, even if it means adjusting some traditions or communication styles. I also think about the effort I'm putting into learning Spanish. It's not easy, and I'm trying to make progress. But in the meantime, I still feel excluded when they speak Spanish around me. It's like I'm being asked to wait until I'm fluent before I can fully participate in family conversations, which seems unfair. Maybe I need to set some boundaries or find a middle ground. For example, I could ask that they speak English when making plans that involve me, or that my boyfriend translates important details in real-time. That way, I don't feel left out or uninformed. But I'm not sure how to bring this up without making my boyfriend defensive again. It's a delicate situation, and I don't want to damage our relationship or his relationship with his family. Perhaps I should also reflect on my own feelings and why I feel so uncomfortable. Is it because I feel excluded, or is there something else? Understanding my own emotions might help me communicate more effectively with my boyfriend and his family. In the end, I think the key is to find a balance where both my needs and his family's needs are respected. It might require some compromise and open communication, but it's worth trying to work through this together.
